paper_metadata.title: From Text to Knowledge: Bridging the Gap with Probabilistic Graphical Models
paper_metadata.venue: Doctoral dissertation, Faculty of Mathematics, Computer Science and Statistics, Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
paper_metadata.abstract: This dissertation develops probabilistic-graphical-model approaches for turning unstructured text into structured knowledge and for discovery in semantically annotated document collections. Its Text2SemRel system uses conditional random fields to extract entities and typed relations and construct a fact-oriented knowledge base; it is applied at scale to construct the literature-derived human gene-disease network (LHGDN). It also presents directed topic-model extensions of LDA for unsupervised modelling of dependencies between documents and semantic annotations.

problem_addressed: The thesis addresses the gap between facts buried in unstructured textual collections and queryable structured knowledge. Its direct Text-to-KG problem is: given typed entities and relations, extract entity mentions and typed relations from text, normalize them to URIs, and arrange the resulting facts as an entity-relationship graph. The principal applied case is extraction of typed human gene-disease associations from biomedical text.

methodology.description: Text2SemRel is a supervised, schema-guided extraction pipeline. First, a document collection is annotated using entity classes and relation types from a conceptual schema. A linear-chain CRF learns NER and semantic-relation-extraction (SRE) labels using lexical, orthographic, word-shape, character n-gram, contextual-window, and dictionary features. The one-step CRF jointly labels entities and relations for encyclopaedic-style text with a known key entity. The cascaded CRF first predicts entities with an NER CRF, passes role features to an SRE CRF, and is used for general free text; when more than two entity mentions are predicted, it examines N-best Viterbi label sequences. Candidate facts are checked against relation domain/range constraints, entity mentions are normalized by strict controlled-vocabulary matching plus a sliding-window expansion/shrinking heuristic, and valid triples are stored. The thesis additionally develops unsupervised Topic-Concept and User-Topic-Concept extensions of LDA for discovery over already semantically annotated document collections; these models are not the Text2SemRel KG-construction component.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: A supplied conceptual schema/semantic data model defines entity classes, binary relation labels, and each relation's domain and range. It constrains fact acceptance so that only schema-consistent pairs are stored. Controlled vocabularies/thesauri provide entity URIs for canonicalization; in the biomedical implementation, disease names and synonyms come from the MeSH C branch and existing Bio2RDF namespaces supply identifiers. The extracted facts can populate a formal ontology and are serialized as RDF/N-triples.

input_output.input_type: Unstructured natural-language text: general free-text sentences, PubMed/MEDLINE abstracts, and GeneRIF biomedical phrases. The broader thesis also uses documents with existing semantic annotations for topic-model-based discovery.
input_output.input_granularity: Sentence-level sequence labeling; documents/collections are processed as collections of sentences. GeneRIF input phrases are concise statements tied to a known Entrez Gene key entity, whereas general free text has no key entity known in advance.
input_output.output_representation: Typed binary entity-relation triples/facts, optionally in canonical URI form, assembled into an entity-relationship graph. The LHGDN implementation stores an RDF graph encoded in N-triples and uses RDF reification to attach provenance (e.g., source PubMed article) and predicted relation type.

models_and_tools: linear-chain Conditional Random Fields (one-step CRF and cascaded CRF)
MALLET CRF implementation with default Gaussian prior
Viterbi-style decoding; N-best Viterbi plus A* backward pass for multi-entity sentences
MeSH disease and chemical/drug controlled vocabularies and relation-keyword dictionaries
Topic-Concept Model and User-Topic-Concept Model (LDA extensions)
datasets: Disease-treatment corpus from MEDLINE 2001/PubMed abstracts: 3,570 sentences, with seven relation types (cure, only disease, only treatment, prevents, side effect, vague, does not cure).

In-house gene-disease GeneRIF corpus: 5,720 phrases from 453 randomly selected Entrez Gene entries; two biologically trained annotators; estimated inter-annotator agreement about 84%; five relation types.
Large-scale LHGDN source: GeneRIF release dated 31 March 2009, 414,241 total phrases, restricted to 178,004 Homo sapiens phrases.
For ontology/dictionary support: MeSH C (disease) branch including names and synonyms; MeSH D (chemicals and drugs) branch for treatments.

metrics: SRE accuracy for the disease-treatment corpus, evaluated with gold entities and with entities predicted by the pipeline.
Exact entity-level precision, recall, and F-score for combined NER+SRE on the GeneRIF corpus; 10-fold cross-validation averages.

LHGDN comparison by counts of genes, diseases, and associations; overlap/coverage; pathway and Gene Ontology homogeneity versus random controls with two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests; power-law goodness-of-fit.
baselines: Disease-treatment task: best graphical model and multilayer neural network results reported by [163].
Gene-disease task: dictionary plus naive rule-based; CRF plus naive rule-based; CRF plus linear SVM; CRF plus feature-selected RBF SVM.
Large-scale comparison resources: OMIM, UniProt, PharmGKB, CTD, and their CURATED union.
evaluation.setting: For disease-treatment extraction, the cascaded CRF is evaluated on the full 3,570-sentence corpus, including sentences with no entities, with 5-fold cross-validation consistent with the cited 80/20 split; SRE is measured both with gold entities and end-to-end predicted entities. For GeneRIF gene-disease extraction, exact entity-level matching and 10-fold cross-validation are used; genes are provided by the associated Entrez Gene ID, so NER reduces to recognizing diseases. For large-scale construction, the cascaded CRF trained on the complete in-house corpus processes 178,004 human GeneRIF phrases and serializes normalized results as LHGDN.

value: Experimental result: on disease-treatment extraction, the cascaded CRF achieved NER recall 69.0%, precision 75.3%, F-score 72.0%; SRE accuracy 96.9% with gold entities and 79.5% end-to-end. This exceeded the cited best graphical model on NER F-score (71.0%) and was close to the cited neural network SRE score (79.6% end-to-end).

Experimental result: on GeneRIF gene-disease extraction, cascaded CRF achieved recall 76.61%, precision 79.46%, and F-score 78.00%, essentially matching feature-selected RBF CRF+SVM (78.03%) and exceeding the one-step CRF (75.90%).
Experimental result: relation-specific cascaded-CRF F-scores were 78.95% Any, 65.02% Unrelated, 78.91% Altered expression, 80.04% Genetic variation, and 71.16% Regulatory modification.

Experimental result: on a feature ablation for one GeneRIF split, the one-step CRF F-score rose from 38.48% with baseline NER features to 75.22% after dictionaries, dictionary-window, start-window, key-entity-neighbourhood, and negation features.
Large-scale result: LHGDN contains 59,342 positive gene-disease association statements, 1,850 diseases, and 6,154 distinct genes.

Review-level inference: the reported scores support the thesis's claim that cascaded CRF is competitive for the two tested biomedical tasks, but are not evidence of performance on arbitrary domains or web-scale text.

value: Author contribution: the thesis provides an end-to-end path from labelled text through extraction, schema filtering, normalization, RDF storage, visualization, and keyword-supported exploration rather than stopping at relation classification.

Experimental result: the cascaded CRF performs competitively with a carefully tuned feature-selected RBF CRF+SVM on GeneRIF (78.00% versus 78.03% F-score) while the authors report roughly tenfold faster training because feature selection is unnecessary.
Author contribution: the schema's relation domain/range constraints and controlled-vocabulary URI normalization make accepted facts usable in canonical, ontology-compatible form.
Experimental result: relational-context features materially improve the one-step model's F-score (38.48% baseline to 75.22% with all tested feature groups).
Author contribution: the large-scale application yields a provenance-enriched RDF network with typed molecular conditions, substantial coverage, and a graph/keyword exploration interface.

Review-level inference: explicit entity recognition plus typed relation extraction, rather than assuming gold entities, makes the reported end-to-end evaluation more relevant to practical Text-to-KG pipelines than relation-only evaluation.

Review-level inference: the large LHGDN counts are extracted statements, not manually curated truth; the study acknowledges false positives and incomplete terminology coverage, so coverage must not be interpreted as validated biological causality.

code_and_data_availability: The thesis reports that the resulting LHGDN is publicly available online and part of the Linked Life Data initiative; it also reports online availability of supplementary annotation guidelines, relation dictionaries, enriched disease-treatment data, and an earlier LHGDN version. The PDF does not report a public source-code repository or a software license for Text2SemRel.
